summary: Clackamas Marion FPA lookout on Lenhart Butte: CCC-built 100-ft tower in 1939, Army AWS post 1942-43, removed or destroyed in 1972; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 100-ft wooden tower with 7x7-ft observation cab and ground house
facts.status_note: Tower and ground house removed (firetower.org) or destroyed (firelookout.com) in 1972; no source describes what remains at the summit

access.note: No source describes public access or the condition of the site today

events.note: Crow's nest on the butte in the 1920s (firelookout.com); decade only, no specific year
CCC built a 100-ft tower, guard station and garage in 1939 (district annual report); Sandy Post gives the new tower as 103 ft
Walter Dodson in charge from mid-July 1939
Army Aircraft Warning Service observer post activated August 30, 1942; deactivated October 1943 (Forest Lookouts gives October 18 in the header and October 16 in the entry)
Inspection letter of September 1, 1942: 7x7-ft cabin on a 110-ft tower, 14x16-ft ground house, 18x18-ft garage
Ed Ballou and his wife on duty at the post
Tom Boothby and family moved to the station on July 1 to spend the summer months (Sandy Post, July 15, 1954)
Burton Blake hired by the fire warden as a lookout on Lenhart Butte
No one on permanent summer duty at the lookout (The Sunday Oregonian, August 1968, as quoted on Forest Lookouts)
Lookout not manned in 1969 because of the moderate fire season
Tower and ground house removed in 1972 (firetower.org); firelookout.com says destroyed in 1972
Registered August 26, 2010 as US 610, OR 51; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 100 ft (firetower.org; 1939 annual report), 103 ft (Sandy Post, 1939) and 110 ft (1942 inspection letter). The brief's 30.5 m (100 ft) is kept; the story reports all three.
firetower.org says removed in 1972; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1972. Not resolved; the story reports both.
The Aircraft Warning Service deactivation is dated October 18, 1943 in the page header and October 16, 1943 in the log entry. The story gives only the month.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 30.5 m matches the 1939 100-ft tower; kept. No source describes the summit today, so access is unknown. The Forest Lookouts site quotes district annual reports and newspapers secondhand. One web search turned up no further Lenhart Butte sources.
